title: Sharp Bounds on Vaccine Waning Ratios with Changing Variants and Exposure-Altered Susceptibility
banked_reason: D0.5.G graded the delivered sensitivity-indexed finite-program result incremental with paper-score ceiling 6 below the field floor; exact computational reduction and an informative K=2 interior-breakdown demonstration require new-proposal re-anchoring.
gap_reasons: The headline machinery is generic finite-program geometry applied to a newly specified response array; the case-margin frontier only compares endpoint codes.
The sole worked example has ratio one for every delta and demonstrates no informative bounds, interior breakdown, substitution failure, or feasible confidence-set computation.

Replace the exponentially large latent-type formulation with a proved exact computational reduction and demonstrate the complete procedure on a nondegenerate K=2 instance with informative bounds and an interior priming-breakdown threshold; this is new-proposal re-anchoring, not a bounded D0 repair.
Panel findings left unrepaired: related_work_omission@thm:perenyi-collapse-boundary and ballast@prop:k2-worked-compatible-lift.
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery built a sensitivity-indexed finite latent-law model for priming after noninfecting exposure, with sharp ratio geometry, dual sign certificates, exact whole-set projection, and a maximal-delta/breakdown theorem. The mathematics reviewer passed the final claims, but the general referee found that the delivered compression remained exponentially large and the only K=2 example was uninformative, reducing the contribution to generic finite-program geometry at incremental tier. A future re-raise must supply a proved computational reduction and a nondegenerate worked instance with informative bounds and an attained interior priming-breakdown threshold, while closing the related-work and ballast findings.
tldr: Changing pathogen variants make early-versus-late vaccine challenge risk depend on one latent coupling of exposures and responses across periods. The response type permits a noninfecting period-one exposure to alter later controlled susceptibility, and \(\delta\in[0,1]\) bounds the altered fraction. The compatible full-law classes, reduced fibers, and sharp ratio images are nested in \(\delta\); hence a nonempty closed sensitivity range \(\mathcal D\) is represented exactly by its largest value \(\bar\delta=\max\mathcal D\), without a continuum closure. Opposite-side linear-program feasibility defines attained sharp priming breakdown points, with dual strict-sign certificates below a finite threshold and a compatible counterlaw at it. Exact multinomial inversion, including \(\Gamma_0(0;\gamma)=\Delta\), gives unconditional whole-set coverage by projecting only through the maximal fiber. The single-variant and Perényi--Stensrud anchors are projection and calibration comparisons, not class inclusions or transfers.
gap: Janvin and Stensrud (2025) give sharp single-pathogen challenge-effect bounds, and Perényi and Stensrud (2025, Section 5) identify a variant-specific time-to-event challenge subtype effect under exposure and proportionality restrictions. Neither gives a sharp common-history ratio set from trial first-infection risks plus external variant-exposure margins when a prior exposure that did not infect may alter later controlled susceptibility, nor an observable sign certificate valid pointwise over a disclosed bound on that priming.
fill: The substantive chain supplies, pointwise in \(\delta\), exact common-history compression, an always-defined extended sharp set, finite attained reciprocal endpoints under the disclosed denominator condition, and a common-law sign dual with compatible counterlaws. A sensitivity-range envelope reports the set and sign conclusion over \(\mathcal D\). Positivity duality, endpoint sign algebra, biological translation, and the \(K=2\) no-priming lift remain audit or calibration results; the collapse, substitution, radius, and exact-inference frontiers remain open.
